# Read-back

One person is cooking lunch for four people, to be ready by 12:30. The dish is a complete meal: lentil soup, salad, and toasted bread, all served together. The cook has two burners (for the soup base and the lentil simmer), one toaster oven (for warming bread), and one stick blender (for pureeing part of the soup). The key temporal constraint is that the salad and bread cannot start until the soup is simmering quietly—the cook can only stand in one place at a time. Within the soup itself, the lentils must simmer 25–40 minutes, then be partially blitzed and kept at a bare simmer. The salad leaves must be dressed only five minutes after the soup returns to the heat, or they will collapse. The bread is toasted and wrapped in cloth, then the table is set. Finally, when all three components are ready, everything is carried to the table together.
